capabilities: Replace the first H1 heading with the new file name after a rename
Skip updates when heading and file name intentionally differ or the metadata cache is stale
disambiguation: Not a bulk file renamer; it only rewrites the note's first H1 heading after a rename, never renames files or inserts headings.
extras: Desktop only; mobile support is listed as a TODO. Includes a troubleshooting section explaining why it does nothing when Obsidian's metadata cache is out of sync.
intentEvidence: There is an alternate plugin, you might want to check out: Obsidian Filename Heading Sync.
motivation: The author prefers keeping the title inside the file contents so the Markdown is self-contained in other editors, and dislikes the more aggressive syncing behaviour of an existing plugin.
problem: When a file is renamed (e.g. after a template fills in '# Untitled'), the H1 heading inside the note still shows the old name, so heading and file name drift apart.

relations.evidence: There is an alternate plugin, you might want to check out: Obsidian Filename Heading Sync.

summary: Heading-sync plugin that updates a note's first H1 to match a new file name after a rename, and leaves it alone otherwise.
